subject: Audit log egress & export SLA / playbook
messages:
From: Julie Park <julie@finvero.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Audit log retention/export options and timelines

Hi Marissa,

Quick question from our compliance team as we prep for an upcoming audit: can you confirm the options Redwood offers for audit/access log retention and bulk export? Specifically we need to know:

- Supported retention windows (minimum/maximum) and whether we can set different retention for admin vs user events.
- Export formats (JSON/NDJSON, syslog, CSV) and whether exports include full event metadata (IP, user_id, token_id).
- Delivery methods (S3 push, signed download, streaming webhook) and any region constraints (we need EU residency options).
- Typical SLA to generate a full export for ~6 months of activity for a mid-sized tenant (estimate: ~120M events).
- Proof-of-deletion options if we later request a deletion of retained logs.

Can you cc the right folks from infra/security? We want a concise playbook we can hand to auditors.

Thanks,
Julie
Sr. Security & Compliance
Finvero
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Julie Park <julie@finvero.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit log retention/export options and timelines

Hi Julie — thanks for the clear list. Summary below; attaching a short playbook (audit_export_playbook.pdf) with procedural steps and examples.

Short answers up front:
- Retention windows: tenant-level configurable retention: 30, 90, 365, and custom ranges up to 7 years where required under a contractual addendum. You can also set separate retention for Admin (longer by default) vs Application (shorter) events via the retention policy UI or API.
- Export formats: NDJSON (recommended), gzipped JSONL, syslog (RFC5424), and CSV for tabular slices. Exports include event timestamp, actor_id (tenant-scoped), actor_type (user/service), IP, region code, event_type, resource_id, and token metadata reference (token_id present but we can redact/obfuscate tokens on request).
- Delivery methods: S3 push (customer bucket or signed temporary upload), signed HTTPS archive download (7-day presigned URL), and streaming webhook for near-real-time forwarding. For very large exports we can do multipart S3 delivery.
- Residency: Exports are generated in the tenant's control plane region. For EU-resident tenants we can produce exports from EU regions only; cross-border copies require a contractual data transfer addendum.
- SLA for export generation: baseline is 72 hours for a standard snapshot for up to 100M events; accelerated delivery (48h or 24h) is available under Dedicated/reserved-capacity customers or as a one-off premium support engagement. We'll size exactly based on event density and compression.
- Proof-of-deletion: we provide a signed deletion manifest + job logs showing object deletions in our storage layer plus a tombstone manifest for internally purged indices. For customer-side buckets, we provide instructions and a signed attest that our copies were destroyed.

Notes / recommendations:
- If you need long-term archival for eDiscovery, we recommend periodic NDJSON snapshots to your S3 bucket (monthly or quarterly); this keeps queryability and provenance.
- For token-level PII concerns: we can redact token strings and provide token_id references; if you need pseudonymization we can provide a reversible KMS-wrapped mapping under an addendum.

I've looped in Karthik and Soojin for export sizing and residency detail. Naomi (legal) can chime in on deletion attestations if needed.

Next steps: I can draft a short mutual-action plan (MAP) with timeline and deliverables. Does Finvero want a 6-month bulk export now, or do you want a rolling monthly snapshot going forward?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0103

Attachment: audit_export_playbook.pdf (PDF, 420KB)
From: Julie Park <julie@finvero.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit log retention/export options and timelines

Marissa — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying items from our side: 

- Residency: we are EU-first. Can you confirm there is no intermediate US egress when generating an export for an EU tenant? We need an end-to-end EU-only export process for the 6-month snapshot.
- Token/pseudonymization: we need to ensure token values are never in exported artifacts. Token_id references are fine but actual token strings must be omitted.
- SLA sizing: 120M events is our rough count for the 6-month window. 72h baseline is OK but can you provide the expected archive size (compressed) and a better estimate of how many worker-hours or GPUs you’ll need so I can raise an internal request?

Also can you include a sample manifest (columns we expect) so our audit team knows what the package looks like.

Thanks — we want to open a formal support ticket and capture the MAP.

Subject: Re: Audit log retention/export options and timelines — MAP & sample manifest

Julie — thanks, noted on the EU-only requirement and token redaction. Below is a proposed mutual action plan (MAP) and a small sample manifest included as an attachment (export_manifest_sample.csv).

Mutual Action Plan (high level)
- Day 0: Confirm scope and sign the handling addendum for EU-only export. We will open support ticket RED-5421 (linked).
- Day 1-2: Export job scheduling and resource reservation (we reserve a dedicated export worker pool for your snapshot to guarantee 48-hour SLA).
- Day 3-4: Export generation and internal validation in EU region (data never leaves EU control plane).
- Day 4-5: Delivery to your EU S3 bucket with multipart upload and signed manifest. You will receive: 
  - NDJSON gz archive(s) split by day
  - export_manifest_sample.csv (CSV manifest with checksums, object paths, event counts)
  - deletion_attestation.json (signed by Redwood once customer confirms receipt and we purge internal temp copies)

Sizing estimate for ~120M events (rough):
- Compression: expect ~6–12GB compressed (NDJSON gz) depending on average event payload; we’ll provide a tighter estimate after a small sample extract.
- Compute: our typical export runs on a pool of 4 worker nodes (CPU-heavy, some GPU if encryption/compression assisted) for 12–36 hours depending on parallelism; with reserved capacity we can hit 24–48 hours reliably.

Token handling
- We will redact token strings from exported events by default and include token_id only. If you need reversible mapping, request the KMS-wrapped mapping addendum.

Next steps and deliverables
1) We will open RED-5421 and request your EU S3 bucket ARN + write permissions (or we can provide a temporary presigned upload).
2) Sign the EU-handling addendum attached to the ticket.
3) We’ll run a 1-day sample extract (free) to validate compression and schema — that will give you exact sizing and final SLA.

Attachments: export_manifest_sample.csv (CSV, 12KB)

If that looks good I’ll schedule the sample extract for tomorrow morning.

Best,
Marissa
